title: Application security testing (SAST/DAST)
goal_html: Groups triage a mixed batch of security findings, sort each into SAST-catchable, DAST-catchable, or human-pentest-only, and justify the sort. Ties to LO 5.5.B, 5.5.C.
steps_html:
1. Each group receives (or works through in the simulation) a shuffled set of findings: some are source-code snippets, some are live-scan results, some are business-logic descriptions.
  2. Groups sort each finding into three piles: SAST, DAST, NEITHER (human pentest needed), and for each finding write one sentence explaining the sorting rule they applied (does it require a running app? does it require reasoning about intent/business rules?).
  3. Groups then design a one-line CI/CD pipeline order (e.g. "SAST on every commit -> DAST against staging before release -> periodic manual pentest") and justify why that order minimizes wasted effort.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: a "static reviewer" argues the SAST case for ambiguous findings, a "dynamic tester" argues the DAST case, and a "pentester" argues for findings that need human judgment. Debate any finding the group disagrees on before recording a final answer.
exit_html: Each group submits: the one finding they debated most, their final classification, and the one-sentence rule that settled it.
